requirement_text.REQ-063: Execute Decision 0006's D1: relocate users, groups and tenant_role from the public schema into each tenant's own Postgres schema via :prefix. Full design: lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md. Full decision record: docs/migration/decisions/0006-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md.

task.description:
Read git diff main...HEAD on this branch. This is a decision-record-driven requirement (Decision 0006 supersedes part of Decision 0003 Dimension B) -- your decision-record-consistency check has unusually concrete material to check against this run, not just a general 'does this look idiomatic' pass.

Specifically check:

1. **Decision-record consistency.** Decision 0006 section 6 states precisely what it supersedes from Decision 0003 (Dimension B's tenant_id-retention clause and its Addendum's write-time derivation mechanism) and precisely what it leaves standing (Dimension B's actual schema-per-tenant isolation choice, Dimensions A and C entirely). Confirm this implementation's actual diff matches that scope exactly -- does anything in this diff touch tenant_id in a way that goes beyond D1 (moving users/groups/tenant_role) into D2 territory (dropping tenant_id, which is REQ-064's job)? The design's own scope boundary says tenant_id is NOT dropped by this work -- verify the diff actually honors that, not just that the design doc says it does.

2. **Migration-file idiom consistency.** The three new create migrations (priv/repo/migrations/20260819000001/2/3_*.exs) should match REQ-022 section 4's prefix()-truthiness guard pattern byte-for-byte in shape with existing tenant-scoped migrations (e.g. priv/repo/migrations/20260818110003_create_tasks.exs) -- not a subtly different reimplementation of the same guard. Spot-check this.

3. **The drop migration's raw-SQL approach.** priv/repo/migrations/20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs uses PL/pgSQL (EXECUTE format(...), a per-row existence loop) rather than Ecto.Migration's DSL -- SECURITY-REVIEWER already passed its INV-7 identifier-safety check, but your job is idiom: is dropping into raw PL/pgSQL for this the right call given this codebase's established conventions, or is there a more idiomatic Ecto-DSL-plus-execute/1 shape this project already uses elsewhere for comparably complex migrations that should have been followed instead? Check docs/anti-patterns.md for any relevant precedent before judging.

4. **Scope creep.** lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.copy_identity_tables.ex are new modules -- confirm they do only what decision 0006 section 4 and the design's section 4 ask for (copy existing public rows into tenant schemas) and don't quietly grow extra functionality (e.g. a general-purpose data-migration framework beyond what this one-time cutover needs).

5. **provision_oidc_user/3 to /4's arity change** -- REVIEWER's own idiom lens on this, separate from SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-8 check: does the new opts :: [prefix: String.t()] parameter match this project's existing definitions.ex convention exactly (not a look-alike reinvention), and is the private call chain's threading consistent with how this project already threads options elsewhere?

Use your standard procedure (.claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions: idiomatic vs. crutch, supervision integrity -- not applicable here, no supervision-tree file touched, confirm that's actually true though -- type-safety gaps, scope creep) plus docs/anti-patterns.md.
acceptance_criteria: Decision 0006/0003 supersession scope confirmed to match the actual diff -- no tenant_id drop present
New migrations' prefix()-guard shape matches existing tenant-scoped migration precedent
Drop migration's raw-SQL/PL-pgSQL approach evaluated for idiom fit, with anti-patterns.md checked
New modules (identity_migration.ex, the Mix task) confirmed scoped to exactly what decision 0006 section 4 asks for, no scope creep
provision_oidc_user's new opts parameter confirmed to match definitions.ex's real convention, not a reinvention
No supervision-tree file touched, confirmed not just assumed

result.summary: REVIEWER PASS on WF02-REQ063's implementation of Decision 0006 D1 (users/groups/tenant_role -> per-tenant schema). All five checked items clear. (1) Decision-record scope: grepped the full diff for DROP COLUMN/tenant_id-removal -- none exists. No Identity.User/Group/TenantRole schema module is even in the changed-files list, so the application-layer tenant_id field is untouched. The three new migrations carry tenant_id forward unchanged (groups, users) or never had it (tenant_role), exactly matching Decision 0006 section 6's supersession boundary (Dimension B's tenant_id-retention clause is what's superseded; the schema-per-tenant isolation choice, Dimensions A/C, is untouched) and the design doc's own explicit 'D2 is REQ-064's job, not this one' statements. (2) Migration idiom: byte-for-byte compared 20260819000001/2/3_*.exs against 20260818110003_create_tasks.exs -- identical `if prefix() do ... create table(..., prefix: prefix())` guard shape, correctly registered in TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migration_manifest. (3) Drop migration (20260819000004): raw PL/pgSQL (DO $$, EXECUTE format(...), per-row existence loop) is idiomatic here -- verified against R-Co's actual GBL-112_tnt01_drop_legacy_public_business_tables.sql, which uses the identical DO $$/DROP TABLE IF EXISTS CASCADE/guard shape; this is a genuine one-off guarded cutover step, not a repeatable schema change, so Ecto.Migration DSL would be the wrong tool. docs/anti-patterns.md has no entry contradicting this. ELIXIR-DEV's substitution of a per-row existence check for R-Co's unavailable onboarding_registry flag was made explicitly and flagged for review rather than silently invented -- correct call, and stronger than a row-count-parity check (catches misrouted rows a count could still balance). (4) Scope creep: identity_migration.ex and the Mix task do exactly copy-groups/copy-users/copy-tenant-roles with on_conflict:-:nothing idempotency and orphan detection for tenant_role's group_id FK -- no generic migration framework, no unrequested extensibility. (5) provision_oidc_user/3->4: read definitions.ex directly (not taken on faith) -- confirmed identical `@type opts :: [prefix: String.t()]` convention and the same Keyword-based threading shape used throughout definitions.ex's create/2, get/2, list_versions/2, etc. One non-blocking divergence: definitions.ex uses `Keyword.get(opts, :prefix)` (nil flows into tenant_id_for_schema_name/1, which has a catch-all clause returning {:error, :invalid_schema_name}), while identity.ex uses `Keyword.fetch!(opts, :prefix)` (raises on omission). This is a deliberate, documented choice (identity.ex's own comment: a missing prefix must never silently resolve against the no-longer-authoritative public schema) and the sole caller (auth_pipeline.ex) always supplies prefix: from an already-resolved schema name, so it is not a look-alike reinvention -- just a stricter failure mode than definitions.ex's, worth watching if a second caller is ever added without threading opts correctly. Supervision integrity: confirmed by grepping the diff's changed-file list for supervisor/process_instance/gen_statem/instance_supervisor -- zero matches. No supervision-tree file was touched; this is a schema/migration/context-module change only.

issues.description: Letflow.Identity's provision_oidc_user/4 call chain uses Keyword.fetch!(opts, :prefix) (raises on missing prefix) where lib/letflow/definitions.ex's established convention uses Keyword.get(opts, :prefix) (nil flows through to tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's catch-all {:error, :invalid_schema_name} clause). Deliberate and documented in identity.ex's own comments, and the sole caller (auth_pipeline.ex) always supplies prefix: from a successfully-resolved schema name, so this is not blocking. Worth a passing note if a second caller of provision_oidc_user/4 is ever added: it will need to supply prefix: explicitly or it will crash rather than degrade to an error tuple.
